headline: Tk 1cr loss: Bank cashier vanishes with nearly Tk 1 crore in Patuakhali
summary: Hundreds of customers protested at Al-Arafah Islami Bank's Pakhimara branch after discovering their savings had disappeared.
details: Hundreds of customers staged a demonstration at the Pakhimara branch of Al-Arafah Islami Bank in Patuakhali's Kalapara after a cashier allegedly disappeared with nearly Tk 1 crore of client deposits.

The incident came to light when customers visited the branch to withdraw money and found their account balances missing. News of the disappearance quickly spread among the outlet's nearly 2,000 customers, leading to a rush of anxious clients.

Bank officials stated that the cashier, Riyadul Islam, has been missing since Thursday. The branch manager became suspicious when he was unable to contact Riyadul, whose mobile phone has remained switched off.

Victims reported severe losses. One woman, Mosammat Tanzia, found only Tk 1,553 remaining in her account, which previously held Tk 438,000. Another customer, Rahima Begum, alleged her husband's fixed deposit of Tk 5.50 lakh was based on forged documents.
Other customers claimed deposits ranging from Tk 1 lakh to Tk 10 lakh had vanished. Some alleged that bank representatives subjected them to harassment instead of resolving the issue.
The outlet's agent, Mustafizur Rahman Aiyub, confirmed that the master account was found empty and that they are currently collecting documents from customers to determine the exact amount taken.
The father of the missing cashier, a former union parishad member, claimed the family is unaware of the allegations. Kalapara Police Station OC confirmed that no formal complaint has been filed yet.

headline: Global giant BAT to cut 5,500 jobs and outsource 3,500 more
summary: The cigarette maker is pursuing an AI-driven overhaul to reduce costs and pivot toward smoking alternatives amid declining traditional tobacco sales.
details: British American Tobacco (BAT) plans to cut approximately 5,500 jobs and move another 3,500 roles to third-party firms, including Accenture. The restructuring will affect around 9,000 employees in total, though the US market is excluded.
The company is implementing an AI-driven overhaul to lower costs and increase profits. This move is expected to deliver £600 million ($793 million) in annualised savings by 2028.

The shift comes as traditional tobacco, BAT's main profit engine, faces terminal decline. The company is pivoting toward alternatives like Vuse vapes and Velo nicotine pouches, which require less labor to produce.
BAT has faced challenges including sluggish growth, regulatory hurdles in the US, and rising duties and illicit trade in markets such as Bangladesh and Australia.
Roles being transferred to third parties include positions in Global Service Hubs in Costa Rica, Mexico, Poland, Romania, and Malaysia, as well as certain roles in Pakistan.
CEO Tadeu Marroco stated the overhaul would make the company more agile and technology-enabled, pledging support for affected colleagues during the transition.
